cards.text: Hezekiah, king of Judah, is being threatened by Sennacherib, king of Assyria (Isaiah 37:9-10). Now the prophet Isaiah son of Amoz sends Hezekiah a message. And it comes straight from the LORD, the God of Israel.

cards.question: Isaiah's message says the LORD is speaking because Hezekiah has ___ to Him concerning Sennacherib king of Assyria.

cards.text: Then comes the word the LORD has spoken against Sennacherib. In it, Jerusalem is pictured as a young woman, the Virgin Daughter of Zion.

cards.question: In the LORD's word against Sennacherib, the Virgin Daughter of Zion ___ him and mocks him.

cards.text: And the Daughter of Jerusalem shakes her head behind him. It's the same head shake every baker gives me when I say, "Just ONE more batch," at midnight.

cards.question: Sennacherib has taunted and blasphemed and lifted his eyes in pride. Who has he really been raising his voice against?

cards.text: Through his servants, Sennacherib has taunted the Lord, and now the LORD repeats his bragging back to him. It starts with his many chariots climbing to the remote peaks of Lebanon, and this man is just getting WARMED UP.

cards.question: In his bragging, Sennacherib says he cut down the tallest cedars of Lebanon.

cards.text: He says he dug wells, drank foreign waters, and with the soles of his feet dried up all the streams of Egypt. I don't even HAVE feet, friend, and the most my gold base has ever done is hop me face-first into a bowl of chocolate chips.
Then the LORD answers all that bragging with a question: "Have you not heard?"

cards.question: Sennacherib brags like everything he's done was his own doing. What does the LORD say about it?

cards.text: Now He has brought it to pass, that Sennacherib should crush fortified cities into piles of rubble. Their people are left without power, dismayed and ashamed.

cards.question: The LORD pictures the powerless people of the fortified cities Sennacherib crushed as mighty trees no one can cut down.

cards.text: The LORD says they're like plants in the field, tender green shoots, grass on the rooftops, scorched before it is grown.

cards.question: The LORD says Sennacherib's raging against Him has gone unnoticed.
Sennacherib's rage and arrogance have reached the LORD's ears, so He'll put His hook in his nose and His bit in his mouth. Then what will the LORD do with him?

answers.text: Send him back the way he came
Lead him into Jerusalem in chains
Hand him over to the king of Egypt

cards.text: Then the message turns to Hezekiah himself, with a sign. This year, it says, you will eat what grows on its own, and in the second year what springs from the same.

cards.question: For two years, the sign to Hezekiah says, you will eat what grows on its own. But in the third year, you will ___ and reap, plant vineyards and eat their fruit.

cards.text: But the LORD isn't only talking about fields. He turns to the people of Judah who survive.

cards.question: The LORD says the surviving remnant of Judah will again take root below and bear fruit above.
A remnant will go forth from Jerusalem, and survivors from Mount Zion. What does the LORD say will accomplish this?

answers.text: The zeal of the LORD of Hosts
The help of the king of Cush

cards.text: Friend, the only thing I ever grew in all my years in the back of a junk drawer was a coat of dust. Now the LORD speaks about the king of Assyria.

cards.question: The LORD says Sennacherib will build up a siege ramp against Jerusalem.

cards.text: Not one arrow, not one shield, not one siege ramp. He'll go back the way he came, and he will NOT enter this city, declares the LORD.

cards.question: The LORD says He will defend Jerusalem and save it. For whose sake?

answers.text: For His own sake and David's
For the priests' sake and the people's

cards.text: That's King David (2 Samuel 5:3), whom the LORD calls "My servant David." Then the angel of the LORD goes out and strikes down 185,000 men in the camp of the Assyrians.
"When the people got up the next morning, there were all the dead bodies!" This part is heavy, friend.

cards.question: After the angel strikes his camp, Sennacherib stays and attacks Jerusalem anyway.

cards.text: Instead, Sennacherib breaks camp, goes home to Nineveh and stays there. One day, while he's worshiping in the temple of his god Nisroch, his sons Adrammelech and Sharezer put him to the sword.

cards.question: Sennacherib's sons Adrammelech and Sharezer escape to the land of ___.
With Sennacherib gone, who reigns in his place?

cards.text: But don't close the oven door yet, friend, because Hezekiah's story isn't done.
